title: Many sheets at once
summary: wb.worksheets is every sheet in order, so a loop can total each branch, or stack every sheet into one. The sheet’s name (ws.title) becomes a column, so nothing is lost when sheets are combined.
objectives: Loop over every sheet with wb.worksheets.
Stack the rows of many sheets into one sheet, with the sheet name as a column.
Split one sheet into a sheet per group.

slides.h: By the end: one sheet from many
slides.say: Each branch of Sharma Traders keeps its own sheet in branches.xlsx. Meera copies them into one by hand every month. By the end of this lesson a loop does it, and totals each branch on the way.
points: `for ws in wb.worksheets:` visits every sheet.
`ws.title` is the sheet’s name: keep it as a column.
p: Each branch of Sharma Traders keeps its own sheet in branches.xlsx. Meera copies them into one by hand every month. By the end of this lesson a loop does it, and totals each branch on the way.
`for ws in wb.worksheets:` visits every sheet.
`ws.title` is the sheet’s name: keep it as a column.

visual.text:
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook("branches.xlsx")
out = openpyxl.Workbook()
allws = out.active
allws.title = "All"
allws.append(["Branch", "Item", "Qty", "Amount"])
for ws in wb.worksheets:
    total = 0
    for item, qty, amount in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True):
        allws.append([ws.title, item, qty, amount])
        total += amount
    print(f"{ws.title}: ₹{total}")
out.save("all_branches.xlsx")

slides.say: The outer loop goes through the sheets; the inner loop goes through one sheet’s rows. A total that belongs to one sheet resets at the start of each sheet.
points: `total = 0` inside the outer loop: one total per sheet.
Before both loops: one total for everything.
p: The outer loop goes through the sheets; the inner loop goes through one sheet’s rows. A total that belongs to one sheet resets at the start of each sheet.
`total = 0` inside the outer loop: one total per sheet.
Before both loops: one total for everything.

slides.say: Splitting is the reverse: go through one sheet and append each row to the sheet for its group, making that sheet the first time a group appears.
p: Splitting is the reverse: go through one sheet and append each row to the sheet for its group, making that sheet the first time a group appears.

visual.text:
import openpyxl
ws = openpyxl.load_workbook("sales.xlsx")["Nov"]
out = openpyxl.Workbook()
out.remove(out.active)
for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True):
    branch = row[1]
    if branch not in out.sheetnames:
        out.create_sheet(branch).append(["Order", "Branch", "Item", "Qty", "Price"])
    out[branch].append(row)
print(out.sheetnames)

tasks.prompt: Split **sales.xlsx** (sheet **Nov**: Order, Branch, Item, Qty, Price) into **by_branch.xlsx** with one sheet per branch, in the order the branches first appear, each with the same header and that branch’s rows. No empty default sheet. Print the sheet names.
tasks.model:
import openpyxl
ws = openpyxl.load_workbook("sales.xlsx")["Nov"]
out = openpyxl.Workbook()
out.remove(out.active)
for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True):
    branch = row[1]
    if branch not in out.sheetnames:
        out.create_sheet(branch).append(["Order", "Branch", "Item", "Qty", "Price"])
    out[branch].append(row)
out.save("by_branch.xlsx")
print(out.sheetnames)
